graph_record_queries.notation: R is a collection of original records; each P is a declared predicate.
graph_record_queries.question: Which records have at least ten connections?

breadth_first_search.notation: The distance is the number of edges in a shortest path; unreachable vertices have no finite distance.
breadth_first_search.question: How many hops connect this person to everyone else?

single_source_shortest_paths.notation: Edge weights w are nonnegative path costs.
single_source_shortest_paths.question: What is the lowest-cost route from this location?

many_source_shortest_paths.notation: D contains shortest-path costs for the requested origins and destinations.
many_source_shortest_paths.question: What are the shortest distances between these locations?

widest_paths.notation: c is edge capacity; a path is only as wide as its smallest capacity.
widest_paths.question: Which route has the largest bottleneck capacity?

temporal_fastest_paths.notation: The set of journeys J obeys edge times. Earliest-arrival mode minimizes arrival time instead of duration.
temporal_fastest_paths.question: What is the fastest time-respecting journey?

top_k_critical_paths_dag.notation: Paths run from declared sources to sinks in a directed acyclic graph; w is delay.
top_k_critical_paths_dag.question: Which dependency paths have the greatest total delay?

hop_constrained_cycle_path_enumeration.notation: The hop length is ell. Cycle mode instead closes a simple path through the requested vertex or edge.
hop_constrained_cycle_path_enumeration.question: List simple paths between these vertices within four hops.

transitive_closure_reachability.notation: The contract declares whether zero-length paths count as reachability.
transitive_closure_reachability.question: Can this vertex reach that vertex?

topological_sort.notation: pi is a vertex ordering; a directed cycle prevents such an ordering.
topological_sort.question: In which order can I process these dependencies?

connected_components.formula: u\sim v\iff u\leadsto v\text{ and }v\leadsto u
connected_components.notation: This defines strong components. Weak components ignore direction before testing connectivity.
connected_components.question: Which groups are disconnected from one another?

biconnected_components.formula: B\text{ remains connected after removing any one vertex}
biconnected_components.notation: Blocks are maximal sets under this condition; bridges and isolated cases follow the contract.
biconnected_components.question: Which single vertices or edges hold this network together?

max_flow_min_cut.notation: Flow respects capacities and conservation. S contains the source and T the sink; optional vertex capacities require the corresponding cut model.
max_flow_min_cut.question: What is the maximum flow between these terminals?

spanning_tree_forest.notation: F spans each connected component without cycles. Maximum mode replaces the minimum with a maximum.
spanning_tree_forest.question: Connect every location at minimum total cost.

group_steiner_tree.notation: T is a connected tree and each G_i is a required group.
group_steiner_tree.question: What is the cheapest tree reaching at least one member of each group?

maximal_clique_enumeration.notation: Maximal means that no vertex can be added; it does not mean largest.
maximal_clique_enumeration.question: Find all fully connected groups that cannot be extended.

maximum_clique.notation: Every pair of selected vertices must be adjacent; the objective is group size.
maximum_clique.question: What is the largest fully connected group?

k_clique_counting_enumeration.notation: k is the exact number of vertices in each clique.
k_clique_counting_enumeration.question: How many fully connected groups of four are there?

maximal_biclique_enumeration.formula: A\subseteq L,\ B\subseteq R,\ A\times B\subseteq E
maximal_biclique_enumeration.notation: A and B form a complete two-sided group and neither side can be enlarged while preserving completeness.
maximal_biclique_enumeration.question: Which groups of users are each connected to every business in a group?

quasi_clique_mining.notation: gamma is the required fraction of possible neighbors inside a group; the contract also sets minimum size and maximality.
quasi_clique_mining.question: Find groups where each member connects to most of the others.

densest_subgraph.notation: C_k counts k-cliques. k=2 gives edges per vertex; weighted k=2 uses the sum of edge weights. k does not fix the result size.
densest_subgraph.question: Find the densest subgraph by edges per vertex.

densest_k_subgraph.notation: Here k fixes the number of selected vertices; unweighted edges have unit value.
densest_k_subgraph.question: Which ten vertices have the greatest induced edge value?

k_core_decomposition.notation: The k-core is the maximal induced subgraph meeting the internal-degree threshold.
k_core_decomposition.question: Find the core where everyone has at least three neighbors inside it.

k_truss_decomposition.notation: Support counts triangles containing an edge within H; a k-truss is maximal under this condition.
k_truss_decomposition.question: Which edges remain in tightly supported triangle groups?

community_detection.notation: P is a partition and Q is the declared community objective. Heuristic profiles do not certify a global optimum.
community_detection.question: Split this network into communities.

seeded_local_community_detection.notation: S_0 is the seed set; a nontrivial feasible set is required and volume follows the contract.
seeded_local_community_detection.question: Find a well-connected community around these seed vertices.

overlapping_community_detection.notation: Each C_i is a k-clique; connected components of this clique-adjacency graph induce overlapping communities.
overlapping_community_detection.question: Find overlapping communities joined through shared cliques.

balanced_graph_partitioning.notation: The partition has a declared number of nonempty parts and balance bounds. Other declared objectives use their own normalization.
balanced_graph_partitioning.question: Split the graph into four balanced groups with few crossing edges.

hypergraph_partitioning.notation: lambda_e counts parts touched by hyperedge e. Connectivity mode uses lambda_e minus one instead; parts must satisfy balance bounds.
hypergraph_partitioning.question: Divide this hypergraph into balanced groups.

signed_network_structural_balance.notation: s is the edge sign. Zero disagreement certifies two-faction balance.
signed_network_structural_balance.question: Can positive and negative relationships be explained by two factions?

centrality_influential_node_mining.notation: c is the chosen centrality, such as degree, PageRank, or betweenness; these measure different forms of importance.
centrality_influential_node_mining.question: Which vertices have the most direct connections?

personalized_pagerank_rwr.notation: s is the seed distribution, alpha the restart probability, and P the declared transition matrix.
personalized_pagerank_rwr.question: Which vertices are most relevant to these seeds?

influence_maximization.notation: A(S) is the activated set under the declared diffusion model. Sampling or heuristic selection does not prove the optimum.
influence_maximization.question: Which seed group is expected to reach the most vertices?

simrank_vertex_similarity.notation: Distinct vertices use the recursive neighbor similarity; self-similarity and empty-neighbor cases follow the contract.
simrank_vertex_similarity.question: Which vertices have similar relationship patterns?

link_prediction.notation: s is the declared structural score, such as common-neighbor count or Jaccard similarity.
link_prediction.question: Which currently missing connections score highest?

graph_edit_distance_mcs.notation: tau is a sequence of edits. Maximum-common-subgraph mode instead maximizes the size of a common subgraph under the declared matching rules.
graph_edit_distance_mcs.question: How many edits separate these two graphs?

network_alignment.notation: M is an admissible vertex mapping; its cardinality, injectivity, weights, and objective are specified by the contract.
network_alignment.question: Which vertices correspond between these networks?

triangle_counting_listing.notation: Each unordered triple is counted once after the contract's normalization.
triangle_counting_listing.question: How many triangles are in this graph?

butterfly_counting_bipartite.notation: Each butterfly has two vertices on each side and all four cross edges.
butterfly_counting_bipartite.question: How many two-by-two complete groups are in this bipartite graph?

graphlet_counting.notation: H is a connected induced graphlet; each vertex subset is counted once by its isomorphism class.
graphlet_counting.question: How many induced graphlets of each shape occur?

graph_motif_counting.notation: The declared motif, inducedness, and symmetry rules define an occurrence.
graph_motif_counting.question: Count occurrences of this small graph pattern.

temporal_motif_mining.notation: An occurrence must match the declared event pattern and its time window; profile-specific ordering rules also apply.
temporal_motif_mining.question: How many ordered interaction patterns occur within this time window?

subgraph_isomorphism.notation: f is injective; induced mode also preserves nonedges, and declared label predicates must hold.
subgraph_isomorphism.question: Find all matches of this query graph.

frequent_subgraph_mining.notation: A pattern is frequent when its graph-collection support reaches the declared threshold; containment follows the contract.
frequent_subgraph_mining.question: Which subgraphs occur in many graphs in this collection?

single_graph_frequent_subgraph_mining.notation: Support uses the declared single-host measure and embedding rules, not automatically a graph-collection count.
single_graph_frequent_subgraph_mining.question: Which labeled subgraphs repeat in this graph?

bipartite_matching_assignment.notation: M is a matching across declared sides; cardinality and minimum-cost modes have distinct objectives.
bipartite_matching_assignment.question: Assign these tasks to workers at minimum cost.

general_graph_weighted_matching.notation: No bipartite partition is assumed. A heuristic profile need not attain the maximum.
general_graph_weighted_matching.question: Choose disjoint pairs with the highest total weight.

maximal_independent_set.notation: S is independent and cannot be enlarged by one vertex; it need not be largest.
maximal_independent_set.question: Find a nonconflicting group that cannot be extended.

maximum_independent_set.notation: The selected vertices have no edges between them and maximum cardinality is the objective.
maximum_independent_set.question: What is the largest group with no internal connections?

minimum_vertex_cover.notation: Every edge must touch a selected vertex.
minimum_vertex_cover.question: What is the smallest set touching every relationship?

vertex_coloring.notation: r is the declared conflict distance. A valid coloring need not use the fewest possible colors.
vertex_coloring.question: Assign nonconflicting colors to connected vertices.

entity_resolution_blocking.notation: Blocking keys b generate candidate pairs; optional confirmation rules determine actual matches.
entity_resolution_blocking.question: Which records should be compared as possible duplicates?

graph_coarsening.notation: This shows sum aggregation; the declared profile controls aggregation, loops, and feature handling.
graph_coarsening.question: Collapse these groups into a smaller graph.

induced_subgraph_ego_extraction.notation: S is explicit or discovered within the requested hop radius around seeds.
induced_subgraph_ego_extraction.question: Show the two-hop neighborhood around this vertex.

knn_graph_construction.notation: The metric, tie handling, and symmetrization are declared parameters.
knn_graph_construction.question: Build a nearest-neighbor graph from these vectors.

spectral_graph_sparsification.notation: This is the target quadratic-form guarantee for all x. The result must disclose what guarantee its profile actually establishes.
spectral_graph_sparsification.question: Make a smaller graph that preserves Laplacian behavior.

neighborhood_sampling.notation: f is the fanout per hop; replacement, weights, types, and temporal rules determine the sampling distribution.
neighborhood_sampling.question: Sample a bounded neighborhood around these seeds.

random_walk_generation.notation: P follows the declared walk rule; biased walks may also depend on the previous vertex.
random_walk_generation.question: Generate random walks starting at these vertices.

graph_layout_force_directed.notation: The declared force model updates these positions; a useful drawing is not a structural optimum certificate.
graph_layout_force_directed.question: Draw this graph with connected vertices pulled together.

graph_laplacian_eigenpairs.notation: L is the combinatorial or symmetric normalized Laplacian specified by the contract.
graph_laplacian_eigenpairs.question: Compute the smallest Laplacian eigenvalues and their vectors.

graph_signal_denoising.notation: y is the observed signal; R is the declared graph-difference regularizer.
graph_signal_denoising.question: Smooth these vertex measurements while respecting the graph.

persistent_homology.notation: The flag-complex filtration yields birth/death intervals over the declared prime field.
persistent_homology.question: When do connected components and holes appear and disappear?

graph_anomaly_detection.notation: phi is the declared feature vector and R the reference for normal behavior; a score is not proof of wrongdoing.
graph_anomaly_detection.question: Which vertices are structurally unusual?

null_model_significance_testing.notation: This illustrates an upper-tail empirical test; the declared null model, tail, and correction define the reported statistic.
null_model_significance_testing.question: Is this graph statistic unusual under a degree-preserving null model?

node_classification_regression.notation: The declared graph model produces labels or numerical targets; held-out evaluation determines predictive performance.
node_classification_regression.question: Predict labels for these vertices using the supplied model settings.

graph_classification_regression.notation: Each graph receives a categorical or numerical prediction.
graph_classification_regression.question: Predict a label for each graph in this collection.

hypergraph_node_learning.notation: H preserves hyperedge incidence; predictions follow the declared hypergraph model.
hypergraph_node_learning.question: Predict vertex labels using these multiway relationships.

graph_condensation.notation: The smaller synthetic graph targets supervised utility; it is not an exact topological copy.
graph_condensation.question: Create a smaller synthetic attributed graph for this prediction task.

graph_based_geolocation.notation: Coordinates are inferred from the declared graph model and known locations; they are estimates.
graph_based_geolocation.question: Estimate locations for vertices without coordinates.

node_embedding.notation: Each row is a learned vertex representation under the declared embedding objective.
node_embedding.question: Represent each vertex with a vector.

knowledge_graph_embedding.notation: The declared embedding model scores typed directed triples; a score is not a verified relationship.
knowledge_graph_embedding.question: Score candidate relationships in this knowledge graph.
